table.title: [Summary of the Military Units over which the Peking Government Claims Authority, April 1921]
table.caption_extra: Headnote printed above the table: "The Chinese Government's official army lists, corrected up to April 1921, give only those organizations which are really or nominally under the control of the Peking Government and make no attempt to indicate the numerical strength, which, of course, varies widely. The following is a summary of the military units over which the Peking Government claims authority :"
transcriber_notes: No column heading printed over the row labels; '[Province]' supplied.

Shansi and Shensi: '(Mixed)' is printed after the Regiments — Inf. figure, running across the Regiments Cav./Art. columns; it is placed in 'Regiments — Cav.'. It qualifies the Inf. regiment figure (2 and 3 respectively).
Suiyuan and Sinkiang: a ditto mark (for '(Mixed)') is printed under '(Mixed)'; transcribed as it appears (',' for Suiyuan, '.,' for Sinkiang).
National Army: the single '1' under Regiments stands under 'Cav.'; Heilungkiang '1' stands under Regiments 'Art.'.

Total row: '76 (in all)', '15 (in all)' and '10 (in all)' are each printed spanning the three Brigade, Regiment and Battalion columns respectively; each is placed in the first column of its group. The 'Estimated Numerical Strength' row likewise has one figure per group (330,000 Divisions; 228,000 Brigades; 12,000 Regiments; 1,300 Battalions), placed in the first column of each group.

Total Divisions 33: reconciles. Brigades '76 (in all)': Mix. 68 + Cav. 2 + Inf. 6 = 76, reconciles. Regiments '15 (in all)': Inf. 13 + Cav. 1 + Art. 1 = 15, reconciles. Battalions '10 (in all)': Inf. 9 + Cav. 1 = 10, reconciles.

table.title: [Units of a Division, with the Ranks and Titles of their Commanders]
table.caption_extra: In the following list the terms for the various units of a division are given, together with the ranks and titles of the officers commanding them. It is in nearly all cases sufficiently good form in addressing an officer to take the term for the unit which he commands and add to it the character "chang." These combinations, constituting forms of address or titles are given in the following list, where it is possible to use them after the characters for the officer's rank.
